card.name: Verb after a sentence-opening infinitive phrase
card.fires_on: The word that ends a sentence-opening 'To + verb ...' phrase, usually 'is' or 'so', right before the claim about what that act amounts to.

modes.label: Linking 'is' after a To-phrase
modes.description: The verb 'is' follows a subject phrase that begins with 'To', and a definition or judgment comes next.
modes.example: To doubt this<< is>> to deny the entire history of computing—to

modes.label: 'so' or other closers of the phrase
modes.description: A short word such as 'so' or an adjective finishes the To-phrase just before the verb.
modes.example: To think<< so>> is a basic misunderstanding of the place of

modes.label: Inside the To-phrase
modes.description: The word falls inside a short 'To X' phrase before the predicate.
modes.example: To<< learn>> means to accept the postulate that life

card.writes: It promotes words that introduce an equating statement such as 'is' or 'means', and suppresses words about punishment or criticism.
card.plain: It fires when a sentence begins with 'To do something' and the next words say what doing it amounts to.
